title.value: Learning to Live with Dale’s Principle: ANNs With Separate Excitatory and Inhibitory Units
title.justification: The paper introduces and elaborates on a novel type of artificial neural network (ANN) model called "Dale’s ANNs (DANNs)," which incorporates separate excitatory and inhibitory units, adhering to Dale’s principle, thus matching the title best.
title.quote: Here, by taking inspiration from feedforward inhibitory interneurons in the brain we show that we can develop ANNs with separate populations of excitatory and inhibitory units that learn just as well as standard ANNs. We call these networks Dale’s ANNs (DANNs).

analysis.description: This research paper discusses the development of artificial neural networks (ANNs) adhering to Dale's principle, which dictates separate excitatory and inhibitory units. The authors propose "Dale’s ANNs (DANNs)" and provide insights that enable DANNs to perform on par with standard ANNs. Specifically, the paper highlights how DANNs relate to normalization schemes and the importance of scaled updates to inhibitory neuron parameters for improved learning.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments to compare the performance of DANNs with standard ANNs and Column-constrained models using datasets like MNIST, indicating an empirical approach.
type.quote: We first compared model performance on the MNIST dataset...we observed that ColumnEi models generalised poorly... where as DANNs performed equivalently to multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) ...

name.justification: The paper focuses on aligning artificial neural networks more closely with biological neural circuits, particularly concerning Dale's principle from neuroscience, aiming to enhance their utility in modeling brain functions.
name.quote: The units in artificial neural networks (ANNs) can be thought of as abstractions of biological neurons, and ANNs are increasingly used in neuroscience research.

name.justification: The paper discusses the development and performance of a novel type of artificial neural network that adheres to biological principles.
name.quote: ...by taking inspiration from feedforward inhibitory interneurons in the brain we show that we can develop ANNs with separate populations of excitatory and inhibitory units...

name.justification: The development of DANNs incorporates engineering aspects of deep learning, such as parameter initialization and scaling updates, to improve learning performance.
name.quote: Altogether, our principle contribution is a novel architecture that obey’s Dale’s principle, and that we show can learn as well as standard ANNs on machine learning benchmark tasks.

name.justification: The work contributes to computational neuroscience by offering biologically plausible models for studying neural computation and plasticity.
name.quote: ...which is important for future work using ANNs as models of the brain.

name.justification: The paper presents Dale’s ANNs as the central model which incorporates separate excitatory and inhibitory units, respecting Dale's principle.
name.quote: We call these networks Dale’s ANNs (DANNs).

is_compared.quote: ...DANNs performed equivalently to multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), and even generalised marginally better.
